experiment: E1/E2: pipeline depth and row batch against the vendor on Ascend950PR
card: npu:1 (no running processes at start, but power 427W / 80C: the vendor absolute drifts)
method: msprof per-kernel device time; the vendor is measured before and after the candidates in one window so the comparison stays within-window
caveat: the vendor absolute here (0.079 ms) differs from the clean 0.0514 ms measured earlier; on a shared machine only the within-window comparison is valid, never the ratio across runs
conclusion: device time is flat at 0.160-0.164 ms across rows 4->6, buffer versions 2->3, pipeline stages 2->3 and threads 256->512. Deeper prefetching and larger row batches do NOT reduce the candidate device time; the ~3x gap to the vendor is structural (data path / algorithm), not these knobs.
decision: KEEP none. threads=512 is 2% faster but well inside noise and doubles max_abs_err to 0.03125; the rest are flat or worse. REVERT all. The next attempt must change the data path (a streaming reduce that never materialises a (rows,tile) fp32 fragment), not the tile/prefetch parameters, per the measured AIV-vector-bound / MTE2-starved attribution.
